description:
FILED s530 (Fable), from the merge probe of s530c.  The INTERPOLATED residue of #3864 (s530c fixed the CODE spellings).

  our %name = (KEY => "kv"); our @name = (7,8,9);
  print "@{name[0,2]}\n";      # perl: 7 9      PCL (main AND s530c's tree): dies "Undefined subroutine &main::name called"
Controls on s530c's tree, all = perl: `${name{KEY}}`, `${name[1]}`, `my @x = @{name[0,2]}` (code).
Not checked yet: "${name{KEY}}" / "${name[1]}" inside a string.
Where: the interpolation path (`Pl/InterpScan.pm` -- interpolation scanning happens there or not at all, standing rule) does not apply #3864's canonicalization (`${NAME{...}}` / `${NAME[...]}` / `@{NAME[...]}` = the element / slice; the one exception `${sub {...}}`).  Route the interpolated braced operand through the SAME point s530c's fix uses (rule 11), not a copy.
LOUD (a die), not silent.

=== DONE (s531c, 2026-11-01) ===
FIXED (commit 9126cf85) in Pl/PExpr/StringInterpolation.pm `_interp_array`, the `@{ EXPR }` arm: it compiled only the GUTS (`name[0,2]` = a call of name).  When the guts start NAME + `[`/`{` and the block is the shape `Pl::PExpr::_block_word_subscript` collapses (asked through `_is_braced_word_subscript` on a fragment of the reference's own text -- rule 11, the ONE predicate #3864 put in PExpr), the WHOLE reference `@{name[0,2]}` goes through the pipeline, then is joined like the other slices.  `"${name{KEY}}"` / `"${name[1]}"` already worked (the scalar arm reparses the whole reference); `"@{[ name() ]}"` and `"${\ name()}"` stay calls.
Probes (scratch/s531c/p/interp1.pl, interp2.pl), all = perl: array slice, hash slice, qualified `@{main::q[0,1]}`, lexical, spaced, expression index, qq{}, heredoc, inside a regex, in an s/// replacement, `$"` honoured, `@{$aoa[1]}` unchanged.
Guard: Pl/t/braced-elem-01.t r17-r22 (all fail on ade297e7).  corpus-diff vs ade297e7: identical (the shape is in no corpus file).
subject: LOUD: interpolated `"@{name[0,2]}"` (and likely "${name{KEY}}") still dies "Undefined subroutine &main::name" -- the string-interpolation residue of #3864 (code spellings fixed by s530c)
